subproblems.title: Integrated gradient bound for the composed cut-off χ∘g (Simon (4c) for one smooth approximant)
subproblems.statement: For all P, m ∈ ℕ, every measure μ on ℝ^P, every m-form ω : ℝ^P → Covector(ℝ^P, m) (an arbitrary DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m; no smoothness or support assumption) with covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for every x, all functions f, g : ℝ^P → ℝ with g differentiable on ℝ^P, every LW ∈ ℝ≥0, every differentiable χ : ℝ → ℝ and all reals t, h, c, δ such that, with K := tsupport ω (the closure of {x | ω(x) ≠ 0}), |g(x) − f(x)| ≤ δ and ‖Dg(x)‖₊ ≤ LW in ℝ≥0 for every x ∈ K (Dg(x) = fderiv ℝ g x; ‖·‖₊ is the operator norm as an element of ℝ≥0), |χ′(s)| ≤ c for every s (χ′ = deriv χ), and χ′(s) = 0 for every s ∉ (t − h, t): in [0, ∞], ∫⁻ ‖Dψ(x)‖₊ · ofReal(covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x))) dμ(x) ≤ ofReal(c) · LW · μ(K ∩ f⁻¹((t − h − δ, t + δ))), where ψ := (y ↦ χ(g(y))) and Dψ(x) = fderiv ℝ ψ x (operator norm, ‖·‖₊ its ℝ≥0 version coerced to ℝ≥0∞).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) (f g : Eucl P → ℝ) (LW : ℝ≥0) (χ : ℝ → ℝ) (t h c δ : ℝ), (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x) ≤ 1) → Differentiable ℝ g → Differentiable ℝ χ → (∀ x ∈ tsupport ω, |g x - f x| ≤ δ) → (∀ x ∈ tsupport ω, ‖fderiv ℝ g x‖₊ ≤ LW) → (∀ s, |deriv χ s| ≤ c) → (∀ s, s ∉ Ioo (t - h) t → deriv χ s = 0) → ∫⁻ x, (‖fderiv ℝ (fun y => χ (g y)) x‖₊ : ℝ≥0∞) * ENNReal.ofReal (covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x)) ∂μ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal c * (LW : ℝ≥0∞) * μ (tsupport ω ∩ f ⁻¹' Ioo (t - h - δ) (t + δ))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Provenance (orientation only; the hypotheses are exactly those of the statement): parent proof, Steps 3 and 4 (Simon's bound (4c) for one smooth approximant g = g_j with accuracy δ = δ_j), extracted for a single function g and an arbitrary accuracy δ. No current, representation or sibling result is used.

Notation. K := tsupport ω; E := K ∩ f⁻¹((t − h − δ, t + δ)); a := ofReal(c)·LW ∈ [0, ∞); ψ := (y ↦ χ(g(y))); |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm(α) for covectors α; ‖·‖ on continuous linear maps is the operator norm and ‖·‖₊ its ℝ≥0 version, coerced to ℝ≥0∞. For a set S, 1_S·a denotes Set.indicator S (fun _ => a).

1. (c ≥ 0.) c ≥ |χ′(0)| ≥ 0 (abs_nonneg and the hypothesis at s = 0).

2. (Pointwise bound.) Claim: for every x ∈ ℝ^P, ‖Dψ(x)‖₊ · ofReal(|ω(x)|) ≤ (1_E·a)(x).
 (a) Let x ∉ K. Then ω(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), so |ω(x)| = covectorEuclideanNorm 0 = 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero) and ofReal 0 = 0. The left side is 0, which is ≤ the right side (simp).
 (b) Let x ∈ K. Since χ is differentiable at g(x) and g is differentiable at x, the chain rule gives Dψ(x) = Dχ(g(x)) ∘ Dg(x) (fderiv_fun_comp x (hχ (g x)) (hg x); equivalently fderiv_comp for χ ∘ g). For the one-variable map χ, ‖Dχ(s)‖ = ‖χ′(s)‖ = |χ′(s)| (norm_deriv_eq_norm_fderiv, Real.norm_eq_abs).
  (b1) If g(x) ∉ (t − h, t), then χ′(g(x)) = 0 by hypothesis, so ‖Dχ(g(x))‖ = 0 and Dχ(g(x)) = 0 (norm_eq_zero). Hence Dψ(x) = 0 ∘ Dg(x) = 0, and the left side is 0 ≤ the right side (simp).
  (b2) If g(x) ∈ (t − h, t), i.e. t − h < g(x) < t: since x ∈ K, |g(x) − f(x)| ≤ δ, i.e. −δ ≤ g(x) − f(x) ≤ δ (abs_le). Hence f(x) ≥ g(x) − δ > t − h − δ and f(x) ≤ g(x) + δ < t + δ (linarith), so x ∈ E and the right side equals a (indicator_of_mem). By the operator-norm bound for compositions (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_comp_le), ‖Dψ(x)‖ ≤ ‖Dχ(g(x))‖·‖Dg(x)‖. Here ‖Dχ(g(x))‖ = |χ′(g(x))| ≤ c, and ‖Dg(x)‖ ≤ LW (the ℝ≥0 hypothesis ‖Dg(x)‖₊ ≤ LW cast to ℝ, exact_mod_cast). Since ‖Dg(x)‖ ≥ 0 and c ≥ 0 (step 1), ‖Dχ(g(x))‖·‖Dg(x)‖ ≤ c·LW (mul_le_mul). In [0, ∞]: ‖Dψ(x)‖₊ = ofReal(‖Dψ(x)‖) (ofReal_norm, since ‖·‖ₑ = ‖·‖₊ by definition) ≤ ofReal(c·LW) (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal) = ofReal(c)·ofReal(LW) = ofReal(c)·LW (ENNReal.ofReal_mul with c ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal_coe_nnreal). Moreover ofReal(|ω(x)|) ≤ 1 because |ω(x)| ≤ 1 (ENNReal.ofReal_le_one). Therefore the left side is ≤ a·1 = a (mul_le_mul', mul_one).

3. (Integration.) By step 2 and monotonicity of the lower Lebesgue integral (lintegral_mono, which needs no measurability), ∫⁻ ‖Dψ(x)‖₊·ofReal(|ω(x)|) dμ(x) ≤ ∫⁻ (1_E·a)(x) dμ(x). For an arbitrary set E (no measurability needed), ∫⁻ 1_E·a dμ ≤ a·μ(E) (lintegral_indicator_const_le). Since a·μ(E) = ofReal(c)·LW·μ(K ∩ f⁻¹((t − h − δ, t + δ))) (multiplication is left-associated), the stated inequality follows. ∎

Remark. No sign condition on h or δ and no measurability of f, g, ω or E is used; every step holds verbatim for arbitrary reals t, h, δ (if δ < 0 the hypothesis |g − f| ≤ δ on K forces K = ∅, and case (a) applies everywhere).
proof_key_steps: Off K = tsupport ω: ω(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport, covectorEuclideanNorm_zero), so the integrand vanishes.
On K: chain rule Dψ(x) = Dχ(g(x)) ∘ Dg(x) (fderiv_fun_comp) and ‖Dχ(s)‖ = |χ′(s)| (norm_deriv_eq_norm_fderiv).
If g(x) ∉ (t − h, t) then Dψ(x) = 0; otherwise x ∈ E (from |g − f| ≤ δ) and ‖Dψ(x)‖₊·ofReal|ω(x)| ≤ ofReal(c)·LW (opNorm_comp_le, |ω| ≤ 1).
lintegral_mono and lintegral_indicator_const_le give ∫⁻ … ≤ ofReal(c)·LW·μ(K ∩ f⁻¹((t − h − δ, t + δ))).

subproblems.title: Continuity from above for the shrinking level bands K ∩ f⁻¹((a − 1/(j+1), b + 1/(j+1)))
subproblems.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ, every measure μ on ℝ^P, every closed set K ⊆ ℝ^P with μ(K) < ∞, every function f : ℝ^P → ℝ that is continuous on K, and all reals a, b: as j → ∞ through ℕ, μ(K ∩ f⁻¹((a − 1/(j+1), b + 1/(j+1)))) → μ(K ∩ f⁻¹([a, b])) in [0, ∞] (open intervals (·,·) = Ioo, closed interval [a, b] = Icc, 1/(j+1) computed in ℝ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (K : Set (Eucl P)) (f : Eucl P → ℝ) (a b : ℝ), IsClosed K → ContinuousOn f K → μ K < ∞ → Tendsto (fun j : ℕ => μ (K ∩ f ⁻¹' Ioo (a - 1 / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) (b + 1 / ((j : ℝ) + 1)))) atTop (𝓝 (μ (K ∩ f ⁻¹' Icc a b)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Provenance (orientation only; the hypotheses are exactly those of the statement): parent proof, Step 6 (the sets E_j and continuity from above), with K = tsupport ω, a = t − h, b = t and δ_j = 1/(j+1); only closedness of K, continuity of f on K and μ(K) < ∞ are used.

Notation. δ_j := 1/((j : ℝ) + 1), so δ_j > 0 (positivity); I_j := (a − δ_j, b + δ_j); E_j := K ∩ f⁻¹(I_j). The statement asserts μ(E_j) → μ(K ∩ f⁻¹([a, b])).

1. (Measurability.) The complement I_jᶜ of the open interval is closed (isOpen_Ioo.isClosed_compl). Since f is continuous on the closed set K, the set K ∩ f⁻¹(I_jᶜ) is closed (ContinuousOn.preimage_isClosed_of_isClosed). Elementwise, x ∈ E_j ⇔ (x ∈ K ∧ f(x) ∈ I_j) ⇔ (x ∈ K ∧ ¬(x ∈ K ∧ f(x) ∉ I_j)), so E_j = K \ (K ∩ f⁻¹(I_jᶜ)) (ext; simp only [mem_inter_iff, mem_preimage, mem_sdiff, mem_compl_iff]; tauto). Closed sets are Borel (IsClosed.measurableSet), so E_j is measurable (MeasurableSet.diff), in particular null-measurable (MeasurableSet.nullMeasurableSet).

2. (Antitone.) Let i ≤ j. Then 0 < (i : ℝ) + 1 ≤ (j : ℝ) + 1, so δ_j ≤ δ_i (one_div_le_one_div_of_le, or gcongr). Hence a − δ_i ≤ a − δ_j and b + δ_j ≤ b + δ_i, so I_j ⊆ I_i and E_j ⊆ E_i (linarith on both endpoint inequalities). Thus j ↦ E_j is antitone.

3. (Intersection.) ⋂_j E_j = K ∩ f⁻¹([a, b]).
 (⊇) If x ∈ K and a ≤ f(x) ≤ b, then for every j, a − δ_j < a ≤ f(x) ≤ b < b + δ_j because δ_j > 0; so x ∈ E_j for every j.
 (⊆) Let x ∈ E_j for every j. Then x ∈ K (take j = 0). Suppose f(x) < a. Then a − f(x) > 0, so there is j with δ_j = 1/((j : ℝ) + 1) < a − f(x) (exists_nat_one_div_lt). Then f(x) < a − δ_j, contradicting a − δ_j < f(x) (x ∈ E_j). Hence a ≤ f(x). Symmetrically, if f(x) > b, choose j with δ_j < f(x) − b (exists_nat_one_div_lt); then f(x) > b + δ_j, contradicting f(x) < b + δ_j. Hence f(x) ≤ b, and x ∈ K ∩ f⁻¹([a, b]).

4. (Finite start.) μ(E_0) ≤ μ(K) < ∞ (measure_mono with inter_subset_left), so μ(E_0) ≠ ∞.

5. (Continuity from above.) The sequence (E_j) is null-measurable (step 1), antitone (step 2) and μ(E_0) ≠ ∞ (step 4), so tendsto_measure_iInter_atTop gives μ(E_j) → μ(⋂_j E_j) as j → ∞. Rewriting ⋂_j E_j with step 3 yields μ(E_j) → μ(K ∩ f⁻¹([a, b])), which is the claim. ∎

Remark. No relation between a and b is required: if a > b, step 3 still holds (both sides are empty), and steps 1–5 apply verbatim.
proof_key_steps: E_j := K ∩ f⁻¹((a − δ_j, b + δ_j)), δ_j = 1/(j+1), equals K \ (K ∩ f⁻¹((a − δ_j, b + δ_j)ᶜ)) and is measurable (ContinuousOn.preimage_isClosed_of_isClosed, K closed).
E_j is antitone because δ_j decreases.
⋂_j E_j = K ∩ f⁻¹([a, b]) (exists_nat_one_div_lt for ⊆; δ_j > 0 for ⊇).
μ(E_0) ≤ μ(K) < ∞, then tendsto_measure_iInter_atTop and rewrite the intersection.

subproblems.title: Dominated convergence for the bounded continuous multipliers χ(g_j) against an integrable density
subproblems.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ, every measure ν on ℝ^P, every ν-integrable F : ℝ^P → ℝ, every set K ⊆ ℝ^P with F(x) = 0 for every x ∉ K, every function f : ℝ^P → ℝ, every sequence (g_j)_{j∈ℕ} of measurable functions ℝ^P → ℝ with g_j(x) → f(x) for every x ∈ K, and every continuous χ : ℝ → ℝ with |χ(s)| ≤ 1 for all s: ∫ χ(g_j(x))·F(x) dν(x) → ∫ χ(f(x))·F(x) dν(x) as j → ∞ (Bochner integrals).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Eucl P)) (F : Eucl P → ℝ) (K : Set (Eucl P)) (f : Eucl P → ℝ) (g : ℕ → Eucl P → ℝ) (χ : ℝ → ℝ), Integrable F ν → (∀ x, x ∉ K → F x = 0) → (∀ j, Measurable (g j)) → (∀ x ∈ K, Tendsto (fun j => g j x) atTop (𝓝 (f x))) → Continuous χ → (∀ s, |χ s| ≤ 1) → Tendsto (fun j => ∫ x, χ (g j x) * F x ∂ν) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, χ (f x) * F x ∂ν))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Provenance (orientation only; the hypotheses are exactly those of the statement): parent proof, Step 7 (σ ↓ 0, here j → ∞, on the left side by dominated convergence), where the parent instantiates F = v₂(ω) resp. F = v₁(dω), K = tsupport ω and g_j = the smooth approximations. Here integrability of F, vanishing of F off K, measurability of g_j and g_j → f on K are hypotheses of this statement.

Apply the dominated convergence theorem (tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence) to F_j(x) := χ(g_j(x))·F(x), limit G(x) := χ(f(x))·F(x), and bound x ↦ ‖F(x)‖ = |F(x)|.

1. (Measurability.) χ is continuous, hence measurable (Continuous.measurable). Since g_j is measurable, χ ∘ g_j is measurable (Measurable.comp), hence a.e.-strongly measurable (Measurable.aestronglyMeasurable). F is integrable, hence a.e.-strongly measurable (Integrable.aestronglyMeasurable). Therefore each F_j = (χ ∘ g_j)·F is a.e.-strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.mul).

2. (Integrable bound.) x ↦ ‖F(x)‖ is ν-integrable (Integrable.norm).

3. (Domination.) For every j and every x: ‖F_j(x)‖ = ‖χ(g_j(x))‖·‖F(x)‖ (norm_mul) and ‖χ(g_j(x))‖ = |χ(g_j(x))| ≤ 1 (Real.norm_eq_abs and the hypothesis), so ‖F_j(x)‖ ≤ 1·‖F(x)‖ = ‖F(x)‖ (gcongr, one_mul). In particular the bound holds ν-a.e. (Eventually.of_forall).

4. (Pointwise convergence everywhere.) Fix x.
 - If x ∈ K, then g_j(x) → f(x) by hypothesis and χ is continuous at f(x) (Continuous.tendsto), so χ(g_j(x)) → χ(f(x)) (Tendsto.comp), and multiplying by the constant F(x) gives F_j(x) → χ(f(x))·F(x) = G(x) (Tendsto.mul_const).
 - If x ∉ K, then F(x) = 0, so F_j(x) = 0 = G(x) for every j and the sequence is constant (simp; tendsto_const_nhds).
 Hence F_j(x) → G(x) for every x, in particular for ν-a.e. x (Eventually.of_forall).

5. (Conclusion.) By steps 1–4 and dominated convergence, ∫ F_j dν → ∫ G dν, i.e. ∫ χ(g_j(x))·F(x) dν(x) → ∫ χ(f(x))·F(x) dν(x). No measurability of f or of G is assumed or needed: the theorem only asks for a.e. convergence of F_j to G. ∎
proof_key_steps: F_j := χ(g_j)·F is a.e.-strongly measurable (χ∘g_j measurable, F integrable).
F_j(x) → χ(f(x))·F(x) for every x: continuity of χ for x ∈ K; F(x) = 0 for x ∉ K.
